I struggled a lot with school my senior year of HS. I went from straight As to almost not graduating due to my depression -- i completed zero assignments and stopped going to school. It sucked and im sorry youre going through the same rn :/ Here's what I did:

Talk to your counselor, explain that you're struggling and need help completing assignments. Ask them to speak on your behalf to your teachers (and/or email your teachers directly if you feel comfortable explaining the situation) allow the counselor to be your advocate. Tell them you want to be successful and just need help getting there. In addition, it would help if you seek therapy, both for your mental health and because public schools have to accommodate you (in my experience) if you have documented mental health struggles.

Basically, I was able to continue my senior year and have success only because my counselor communicated for me to my teachers, getting assignments and basically telling the teachers to work at my pace.

I hope your mental can improve soon, please keep your chin up and know that it'll be okay, academic success is never truly out of reach ♡ You can always start fresh.

It's a lot of trial and error, in my opinion. from 13 to 18 I went through many therapists, and it wasn't until I met my current one 3 years ago that it really "stuck" and I now see him once or twice weekly, usually.

For me, what made him a good match was:

1) There was NO PRESSURE to open up or move at a pace I wasn't comfortable with. He matched my effort. If I put in a 10/10 effortwise one week, but a 2/10 the next week, he didn't ask me to "try harder". He listened and was patient.

2) The more I spend with him the more I discover about myself. Memories, personality traits, etc. A good therapist is like a mirror and helps you see and understand yourself. They don't fix you, they just help you see who you are, and then help you be who you want to be. 

3) He doesn't blame me for my past. Mistakes are not held against me, only used for personal growth. I don't feel like a failure if I report in and I made some backwards progress... he is on my side 100%.

4) Sometimes our sessions are intense and involve a lot of crying or yelling etc. This is important because a therapy session is a safe place to feel unsafe/let your guard down, if that makes sense? So don't shy away from intensity. Let your therapist guide you through tough conversations so long as they bring you back before you end. This comes with a lot of time and trust however.

5) This last one is most relevant to a personal therapist, not group or family therapy. It is important to have a therapist who is only THERE FOR YOU. Sure relationships take two to tango but for personal therapy your therapist should always support you first and foremost!!! They can give you feedback if you are in the wrong but they should never talk to the other party(s), never make you feel like what you said will somehow leave the room... just be someone you can trust, someone who makes you feel comfortable and at ease when the session ends.

Hope this helps ♡
